title: Interpretable machine learning links airway mucins and keratinization to severe asthma
summary: Applying the interpretable machine learning tool SLIDE to airway epithelium transcriptomes, the authors found latent factors that distinguished severe from mild-moderate asthma. High expression of MUC1 and MUC4 and a keratinization program (KRT16) were identified in severe asthma and were inversely associated with lung function in two cohorts. Imaging of endobronchial biopsies showed higher KRT16 protein in severe asthma that correlated with MUC1. Cohort sizes were not stated in the abstract reviewed.
ai_technology: SLIDE, an interpretable machine learning tool that finds latent factors (gene co-expression networks) in transcriptomes
organization: Division of Pulmonary, Allergy, Sleep, and Critical Care Medicine, Department of Medicine (institution not stated in the reviewed metadata)

evidence.tested: Airway epithelium transcriptomes, association with lung function in two asthma cohorts, and imaging of endobronchial biopsy protein expression.
evidence.unknown: Cohort sizes and causal role of the mucins; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Extracts latent gene co-expression factors that separate severe from mild-moderate asthma, pointing to MUC1, MUC4 and KRT16.
